chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created Adam (peace be upon him) from clay, so He made clay forbidden for his descendants.

key_terms.آدَمُ: Adam (peace be upon him), the first human
key_terms.الطِّينِ: Clay, the substance from which Adam was created
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: The Mighty and Majestic, an honorific for Allah

ai.seo_question: Why is clay considered forbidden for humans in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the physical origin of Adam (AS) from clay to a specific ritual prohibition, often interpreted by Shia jurists as forbidding the consumption of clay or its use in specific ritual contexts. This establishes a theological principle where the substance of creation dictates the status of its use for the progeny, reinforcing the concept of *fitrah* (innate nature) in Shia jurisprudence. The narration serves as a foundational text for understanding how physical origins influence ritual purity and dietary laws.
